findings.title: utm_data is an arbitrary user-controlled jsonb hash; an ActiveJob reserved key inside it makes PosthogTrackJob.perform_later raise ActiveJob::SerializationError out of SubscriptionEvent#handle_after_commit_on_create — on the trial_started writer that raise escapes Organization#update! and loses Discord::NotifyFreeTrialStartedJob
findings.evidence: Live, RAILS_ENV=test, queue_adapter :test, org 37139 owner 41118. Set User#utm_data = {"_aj_globalid"=>"x", "utm_term"=>"boots"} via update_columns, then drove the REAL writer: Organization.find(id).update!(stripe_subscription_status: 'trialing', stripe_subscription_id: 'sub_qa5_a7_poison') (the nil -> 'trialing' branch, organization.rb:1128-1134). Observed: update! RAISED `ActiveJob::SerializationError: Can't serialize a Hash with reserved key "_aj_globalid"` out to the caller (X1). The org columns still persisted (after_commit is post-commit; X2) and the SubscriptionEvent row was still created (X3), but the enqueue list after the raise was ONLY ["Notification::FreeTrialStartedJob"] — Discord::NotifyFreeTrialStartedJob was NOT enqueued (X4), because the raise happens in enqueue_posthog_track which runs before the Discord line in the if/elsif chain (subscription_event.rb:41-42). All five ActiveJob 6.1.7.7 reserved keys reproduce it (X5): _aj_globalid, _aj_symbol_keys, _aj_ruby2_keywords, _aj_hash_with_indifferent_access, _aj_serialized (activejob-6.1.7.7/lib/active_job/arguments.rb:51-68). Control with an ordinary key {"utm_term"=>"boots"}: no raise, 1 PosthogTrackJob enqueued (X6).
findings.blast_radius: trial_started writer (organization.rb:1131) is NOT rescue-wrapped, so the exception propagates out of Organization#handle_after_commit_on_update to whatever called update! (sync_with_stripe / the subscription-created webhook branch / the checkout request cycle). The two webhook writers ARE rescue-wrapped (stripe_webhook_handler_job.rb:212-222 and :313-328 `rescue StandardError`), so there the same error is caught and logged — but the ledger row exists while BOTH the PostHog conversion event and Discord::NotifyTrialConvertedToPaidJob are silently lost (the Discord line at subscription_event.rb:45 sits after enqueue_posthog_track).
findings.reachability: The browser signup path cannot produce it: app/javascript/shared/lib/utils.js:192-208 filters utm_data keys to `key.indexOf("utm_") === 0` and caps at 10. The BACKEND does not: Api::V1::RegistrationsController#sign_up_params (registrations_controller.rb:328) permits `utm_data: {}` with no key restriction and assigns it verbatim at :99/:121; Api::V1::OrganizationsController#create copies current_user.utm_data onto the Organization (:34); Api::V1::Users::OmniauthCallbacksController passes merged_tracking['utm_data'] through (:28). So any client POSTing directly to the public signup endpoint with utm_data[_aj_globalid]=x poisons its own org's trial-start path.
findings.note_on_severity: utm_data is in the payload exactly as SPEC 7 specifies, so this is a defect in the design rather than a deviation from it — but the observed runtime behavior is an exception escaping a load-bearing Organization#update! plus a lost Discord notification, which is why it is filed HIGH rather than MED. Minimum fix is scoped to this feature's own code (subscription_event.rb) — no shared-infrastructure change is implied.

findings.title: PosthogTrackJob#perform's pre-existing properties.deep_symbolize_keys also symbolizes the NESTED utm_data keys — no wire consequence, verified
findings.evidence: utm_data {"gclid"=>"abc", "nested"=>{"k"=>"v"}} survives ActiveJob serialize/deserialize with String keys intact, then deep_symbolize_keys turns it into {:gclid=>"abc", :nested=>{:k=>"v"}} before Posthog::Track. posthog-ruby 2.11.0 serializes with JSON.generate (message_batch.rb:22, transport.rb:118), so the wire bytes are identical: JSON.generate(db_value) == JSON.generate(captured_value) asserted and PASSED (T1k). No action; recorded only so a future reader does not mistake the in-memory shape change for data loss.

verified: OWNER-FIRST FALLBACK MATRIX, all 13 attribution fields (utm_source, utm_campaign, utm_data, internal_ref, google_click_id, adroll_click_id, adroll_first_party_cookie, fbclid, fbp, fbc, li_fat_id, ga_client_id, ga_session_id), live on org 37137 / owner 41111 with real DB rows and real enqueued PosthogTrackJob args (ActiveJob::Arguments.deserialize of the TestAdapter entry): (A) owner present + org present -> OWNER value for all 13 (e.g. utm_source 'owner_utm_source' not 'org_utm_source'); (B) owner nil + org present -> ORG value for all 13; (C) both nil -> all 13 keys ABSENT from the properties hash, key set reduced to [stripe_customer_id, to_plan]; (D) owner blank ('' for the 12 string columns, {} for jsonb utm_data) + org present -> ORG value for all 13, proving `present?` semantics not `nil?`; (E) owner present + org nil -> OWNER value for all 13; (F) owner blank + org blank -> all 13 keys ABSENT. 27-check script, 25 PASS; the 2 non-passes are the single utm_data nested-key symbolization noted as A7-L1 (wire-identical).

Cell D precondition asserted separately (D0, PASS): after update_columns the owner's 13 values really persisted as blank-but-not-nil — each read back with nil? == false and present? == false, so cell D exercises the present?/nil? distinction rather than an accidental nil.

SCHEMA: all 13 attribution columns exist on BOTH users and organizations (User.columns_hash / Organization.columns_hash read live). 12 are `character varying`; utm_data is `jsonb` on both. No field exists on only one of the two tables.

utm_data specifically: a populated hash is present? true and lands in the payload as the REAL hash, unmangled and un-stringified ({'src'=>'owner','n'=>1} in DB -> same Hash in the enqueued args, Hash class both sides, T1c/G PASS). Empty hash {} is present? false, so it falls through to the organization value (cell D) and is dropped by .compact when both sides are {} (cell F). Non-hash jsonb shapes also pass through without raising: ARRAY [{'a'=>1},'b'] and SCALAR 'plain string' both reached capture unchanged with wire JSON identical to the DB value (E2, E3 PASS).

PAYLOAD COMPOSITION: conversion row with amount 12345, stripe_subscription_id 'sub_qa5_a7_row', to_plan 'plan_qa5_a7_row_to_plan' on an org whose plan was 'plan_simple_ats_free' and stripe_customer_id 'cus_qa5_a7_from_org' produced exactly {amount: 12345, stripe_subscription_id: 'sub_qa5_a7_row', to_plan: 'plan_qa5_a7_row_to_plan', stripe_customer_id: 'cus_qa5_a7_from_org'} — to_plan deliberately made to DIFFER from organization.plan to prove the ROW is the source, not the org (H2 PASS); stripe_customer_id proven to come from the ORGANIZATION.

amount is present only when the row carries one: a trial_started row with no amount and no stripe_subscription_id produced key set exactly [stripe_customer_id, to_plan] — :amount and :stripe_subscription_id both absent (I PASS). amount: 0 IS kept with value 0 (J PASS) — .compact drops only nil, so a $0 row would still send amount: 0 (no fabrication either way).

Nil sources are never fabricated: with organization.stripe_customer_id nil and the row's to_plan / stripe_subscription_id / amount all nil, all four keys are ABSENT (T3a PASS), and the payload contained zero values equal to 0, '' or {} (T3c PASS).

email / organization_id / organization_name / plan are NOT in the enqueued feature properties (H3 PASS, zero of the four present) and no key named groups, $set or $set_once appears anywhere in the payload (H4 PASS).

Posthog::Track#default_properties LIVE really supplies all four: {email: 'rezu.may@wrkhq.com', organization_id: 37138, organization_name: 'Acme Inc.', plan: 'plan_simple_ats_free'} — asserted against the actual owner/org records (L, T1g PASS). Zero key collision between default_properties and the feature's properties (M PASS: intersection empty; note to_plan and plan are distinct keys, both survive).

ENQUEUE SHAPE for all four written types: PosthogTrackJob enqueued exactly once each, arg0 == 41111 == organization.owner.id and NOT organization.id (asserted explicitly, org id was 37137), arg1 == the enum string matching event_type exactly: 'trial_started', 'trial_converted_to_paid', 'converted_to_paid', 'canceled_subscription' (K x4 PASS).

END-TO-END INTO capture, POSTHOG_CLIENT stubbed with a recorder double via stub_const and guarded by `raise unless POSTHOG_CLIENT.equal?(recorder)` before any capture could run — ZERO real network sends. NOTE for later agents: POSTHOG_CLIENT is NOT nil in the test env; it is a live PostHog::Client (Variables::POSTHOG_API_KEY is present, config/initializers/posthog.rb:5), so any unstubbed Posthog::Track#track in a runner script WOULD send. Driving PosthogTrackJob.perform_now with the real deserialized enqueue args produced exactly one capture (N PASS) with distinct_id == '41112' (String, == owner.id.to_s), event == 'trial_started' (O, T1f PASS), top-level keys exactly [distinct_id, event, properties] — no groups, no $set (Q PASS), and properties == default_properties.merge(feature properties) with every default value and every scalar feature value byte-identical (T1g/T1h/T1i/R PASS; the only diff was the utm_data nested-key symbolization of A7-L1).

posthog-ruby 2.11.0 does not overwrite any feature key: PostHog::FieldParser.parse_common_fields injects only '$lib' and '$lib_version' into common[:properties] (field_parser.rb:131-141), and parse_for_capture only adds '$groups' when a groups: argument is passed, which this feature never passes.

FULL PRODUCTION CHAIN exercised once end to end on the real writer: Organization.find(id).update!(stripe_subscription_status: nil -> 'trialing', stripe_subscription_id: 'sub_qa5_a7_real_trial') -> organization.rb:1128-1134 branch -> CreateSubscriptionEvent -> SubscriptionEvent row (stripe_subscription_id 'sub_qa5_a7_real_trial', amount nil, to_plan == org plan) -> after_commit -> exactly 1 PosthogTrackJob with arg0 == owner id -> deserialize -> Posthog::Track -> stubbed capture. Payload carried OWNER attribution while the ORG also had values set (owner won), plus the org's stripe_customer_id 'cus_qa5_a7_e2e_org' (T1a-T1i PASS).

OWNER, not any org user: a second (non-owner) user in the same org (id 41113 of 4 users) was given attribution values prefixed 'other_'; zero 'other_'-prefixed values appeared anywhere in the payload (T1d PASS) — the code reads organization.owner specifically.

NO STRIPE CALLS at fan-out (SPEC 7 'DB-local data only'): Stripe::Subscription.retrieve, Stripe::Customer.retrieve and Stripe::Invoice.retrieve were all stubbed to raise; creating a converted_to_paid row and performing the resulting PosthogTrackJob completed with no error and produced 1 capture (T2 PASS).

NO-OWNER BAIL-OUT re-confirmed twice: with organization.owner_id nil'd, a converted_to_paid row produced ZERO enqueued jobs at all (S PASS), and a trial_converted_to_paid row produced ZERO PosthogTrackJob while Discord::NotifyTrialConvertedToPaidJob still enqueued (T4 PASS) — the `return unless organization&.owner` guard is scoped to PostHog only, matching SPEC 7.
A utm_data key named '$set' stays NESTED under the utm_data property and does not become a top-level $set on the capture payload (E5 PASS).
SPEC 11.6 (rollout misclassification) was NOT exercised and is NOT filed — it is the disclosed open question for Jessica.
